rule.text:
# Outcome rule for matched wall-treatment contrasts (version 1)

Written on 19 November 2026 before any reading made under it. Level 2 settled which
published contrasts hold the grid, outer closure, numerics and forcing fixed while the
wall treatment or its implementation changes, and compare the arms with one reference
(the member contrasts of `data/revision/wall_change_contrasts.json`). This rule says
what a reader records about the *outcome* of each such contrast. A script derives every
category and count from the recorded rows. Readers do not type a category of a contrast.

The question: when only the wall treatment changes, does the same arm lie closer to the
reference on every quantity the source compares, or does the order of the arms depend
on the quantity, the condition or the region?

## 1. Units

- **Contrast.** One member record (tier strict or broad, in a counted work). Its `arms`
  list is taken unchanged from the Level-2 record and is numbered from 0 in that order.
- **Pair.** Arm 0 with each other arm *j* of the list. The list order was fixed at
  Level 2. Arm 0 is not assumed to be a baseline.
- **Condition.** One repetition of the contrast in which both arms of a pair were run
  under the same controls: one grid, one Reynolds number, one outer closure, one case
  variant. The reader lists the conditions the source displays and gives each a short
  identifier. A streamwise station or a wall-normal position is not a condition. It is
  part of the support of a row.
- **Row.** One quantity, for one set of conditions, at one source location (a figure
  panel or a table), with the order of the arms it shows. A row is written only when the
  source displays or tabulates the arms concerned together with the reference for that
  quantity. A quantity shown without the reference gives no row.

## 2. Quantity classes

Each row has exactly one class.

| Code | Contents |
|---|---|
| `wall_stress` | wall shear stress, skin-friction coefficient, friction velocity, friction Reynolds number when it is an output, friction drag |
| `separation` | separation point, reattachment point, length or extent of a mean separation bubble, when given as a location or length |
| `mean_velocity` | mean velocity profiles, bulk or centreline velocity, flow rate, displacement or momentum thickness, shape factor |
| `pressure` | wall-pressure coefficient, pressure drop, pressure distribution |
| `turbulence` | Reynolds stresses, root-mean-square fluctuations, turbulent kinetic energy, resolved or modelled |
| `load` | lift, total drag or moment coefficient of a body |
| `heat` | wall heat flux, Nusselt or Stanton number, mean temperature |
| `other` | anything else compared with the reference (spectra, flow angle, budget terms) |

`heat` rows are recorded and kept out of every hydrodynamic count. A profile in wall
units (U+ against y+) belongs to `mean_velocity`, although its scaling uses the friction
velocity. If the source tabulates a separation or reattachment location, or marks it so
that it can be read as a number, it gets its own `separation` row besides the friction
curve it comes from.

## 3. Direction of one pair in one row

The direction says which arm of the pair lies closer to the reference: `0`, `j`,
`region` or `unresolved`.

**Tabulated values.** The reader copies the printed strings of both arms and of the
reference (or the printed errors). A script decides the direction with the digit
interval rule of `code/resolve_directions.py`: a printed number stands for every value
that rounds to it, and a direction is resolved only if it holds for every such value.
If the source gives several references for the row, the direction must hold against
each. Otherwise the row is `reference-dependent`. The reader's own judgement of a
tabulated row is not used.

**Plotted values.** Render the page at 200 dpi or more.

- At one location, the discrepancy of an arm is its distance from the reference curve
  or symbol. One arm is *resolved closer* there if its discrepancy is smaller than the
  other's by more than the stroke width of the curves, or the symbol size where the
  arms or the reference are drawn as symbols.
- Scalar read from a plot (one point per arm): the direction is the resolved closer
  arm, else `unresolved`.
- Curve over a support (along the wall, or across the layer): `0` or `j` if that arm
  is resolved closer over more than half of the displayed support and the other arm is
  resolved closer nowhere over a stretch the reader can name. `region` if each arm is
  resolved closer over a nameable stretch. The reader names the stretches in the
  units of the axis. `unresolved` otherwise.
- Several panels or stations of one quantity under one condition form one row. Each
  station is a stretch of the support.
- If the reference is drawn with scatter or error bars, the stroke width is replaced by
  that scatter or bar.
- If the two arms are drawn in different panels with identical axes and the same
  reference, the reader may compare across panels and must say so. The row is then
  resolved only if the difference exceeds three stroke widths.

**Not usable.** A row is `not_comparable` if the arms concerned are not both shown
with the reference for that quantity, if the reference is only another model, or if the
image cannot be read. The reader says which.

## 4. What else is recorded

For each contrast:

- `arm_roles`: for each arm, `baseline` if the source calls it the baseline, standard,
  conventional, existing, default or reference treatment, or introduces another arm of
  the contrast as its improvement, `proposed` if the source presents it as new,
  improved, modified or proposed, or as the treatment under test, else `neither`. One
  located quotation supports the roles.
- For each pair, `theme`: what distinguishes arm *j* from arm 0. One code.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `balance` | one arm retains pressure-gradient, convective or unsteady terms of the near-wall momentum balance that the other neglects (equilibrium against non-equilibrium), both analytic or numerical, neither trained |
| `inputs` | the same or a similar law is given different information: time-filtered or averaged input, relaxation or history terms, further or different input variables |
| `location` | a different sampling or matching height, exchange location or interface position |
| `imposition` | a different way of imposing the model's output or coupling it to the solver (stress against viscosity, slip against traction, weak against strong, flux or gradient correction, enrichment of the solution space) |
| `law` | a different algebraic or analytic law at the same level of physics (two equilibrium laws, two wall functions) |
| `learned` | a trained treatment against an analytic one, or two trained treatments that differ in training data, inputs or architecture |
| `parameter` | the same treatment with a different value of a coefficient |
| `on_off` | a wall treatment against none on the same grid |
| `resolution` | a wall function against a treatment that integrates through the near-wall layer on the same grid (low-Reynolds-number, two-layer, enhanced, zonal or embedded) |
| `other` | none of these |

- `author_statement` on each row: what the source says about that comparison, quoted,
  or `none`. It is stored beside the reading and never merged with it.

## 5. Derived categories (by script)

Orientation. In a pair whose arms have exactly one `baseline` role, the other arm is
the *alternative* and directions are restated as `closer` (alternative closer),
`farther`, `region`, `unresolved`. Other pairs are unoriented and enter only the
symmetric categories.

A row is *resolved* for a pair if its direction is `0`, `j` or `region`.

Pair category over its hydrodynamic rows:

- `one order`: at least one resolved row, every resolved row names the same arm, no
  `region` and no `reference-dependent` row;
- `order changes`: resolved rows name different arms, or a row is `region`;
- `reference-dependent only`: no row names an arm and at least one is reference-dependent;
- `nothing resolved`: no resolved row.

Contrast category: `order changes` if any pair is; else `one order` if any pair is;
else `nothing resolved`.

Where the order changes (not exclusive):

- *between quantities*: two rows of different classes that share a condition name
  different arms;
- *between conditions*: two rows of one class name different arms under different
  conditions;
- *within a profile*: a `region` row.

Estimands, each on the three Level-2 bases (collection, without boundary cases, within
the primary scope), at contrast, work and study-family level:

- **E1**: contrasts by category.
- **E2**: among contrasts in which some pair has resolved rows of two or more classes
  under a shared condition, those with a change between quantities. The classes
  involved are tabulated.
- **E3**: E1 and E2 by theme, and oriented pair categories (alternative closer on every
  resolved row, order changes, baseline closer on every resolved row) by theme and by
  the transfer status of a fitted alternative in `transfer_exposure.json`, where a
  transfer record of the same work names that treatment and flow.

Bounds. Every share is given with the range it could take if each unresolved or
reference-dependent row had gone either way: a contrast counts as `one order` at the
lower bound only if every row of every pair is resolved.

Work and family level. A work is `order changes` if any of its contrasts is. Families
are those of `data/revision/study_families.json`.

## 6. What the counts can and cannot say

The 115 works are a retrieved collection. The counts describe the member contrasts of
that collection. Authors choose which quantities and treatments to show, and treatments
that improve something are more likely to be published. The share of contrasts in
which an alternative is closer is therefore expected to be high, and is weak evidence.
The cells in which the order changes or the alternative is farther carry the
information. None of these counts estimates a frequency for the literature.

clarification.text:
# Clarification O1 to the outcome rule

Written 2026-11-19T14:41:09Z, while the readings ran and before any answer was harvested or opened.
It fills two cases that Section 5 of the frozen rule leaves undefined. It changes no reader instruction.

1. A pair whose resolved rows all name one arm and which also has a reference-dependent row.
   Section 5 excludes it from `one order` and places it in no other category. It is counted
   `one order` at the point value. Like a pair with an unresolved row, it does not count as
   `one order` in the lower bound.
2. A pair whose order changes between two rows of one quantity class under one condition (two
   quantities of the same class, for example two walls or two stress components). The pair is
   `order changes` by the rule. The place of the change gets a fourth label, `within a class`.

The readers' vocabulary writes the closer arm as its index. The script stores `first` for arm 0
and `other` for arm j.

Tabulated rows carry the printed strings and their direction is decided by script.
